fixture.promql_oracle: avg by(scope)(avg_over_time(tslab_r02_periodic[4h])) at final timestamp, independent Python series means; all phases equal within 1e-8

method: Single GitHub Ubuntu runner, four complete fresh server processes in A/B/B/A order; each identical sequence of 96 chronological 4000-row INSERTs under STOP MERGES for inner TAGS/SAMPLES/TimeRanges; /proc process tree watchdog+child worker CPU/IO deltas before and after write; START MERGES+3 OPTIMIZE FINAL CPU/IO measured separately. All 96 QueryFinish records per phase and physical counts verified. Same full native 4h PromQL and exact independent labels/timestamps/numeric values, no caching, no production writes. A/A drift bound predeclared<=25%.
math_bound: Raw UUID vs LowCardinality(UUID) physical representation has dictionary overhead. DistinctID/physicalID rows 66000/68000 ~0.97 after merging, so dictionary overhead may exceed savings when individual series have few bucketed rows. One 0.01s CPU tick is <0.3% of this 5.4s write interval, unlike 12-batch test where it was ~4%; observed raw/LC CPU ratios .8427 for insert and .7118 for merges exceed A/A drifts by large margins. This does NOT imply production effect due O1/glibc and background merge isolation.
limitations: One runner and one ABBA with two phases/mode; cannot claim robust cross-host effect. Two independent-runner replicas are in CI 41624764688; do not invent results.
Server uses stock O1 lab build and glibc, not optimized production allocator/binary.
Background merges stopped during inserts, then restarted and forced to final; this separates phases but does not test natural concurrent reads+writes/merges.
/proc write_bytes includes non-physical-table writes, not billable storage cost; merged compressed bytes and marked physical rows are authoritative small-fixture size.
Native read measured for parity but no concurrent query latency p95; cannot use these write results as read-path proof.
